Skill patched. I added a dedicated section for TIPS inflation-adjusted price volatility covering the key generalizable points:

1. Adjusted price = quoted price × index ratio (the inflation-accounting step unique to TIPS)
2. Population std dev (pstdev, ÷N) vs sample std dev (÷N-1) — the most likely arithmetic trap
3. Exact coupon matching (2-3/8% = 2.375%) when multiple TIPS exist
4. Using all reporting dates in the window with both endpoints

The core lesson here that generalizes beyond this one question: when an OfficeQA question says "population standard deviation," it's signaling pstdev not stdev, and "adjusted price accounting for index ratios" means multiply by the index ratio before any statistics. Those two cues will recur for other volatility-style questions.

No memory update needed — the skill section captures it better than a flat fact would.
